title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: This work combines a sequence-to-sequence language model with retrieved Wikipedia passages. A dense index provides external evidence alongside knowledge stored in model parameters. It compares retrieval shared across an answer with retrieval that can vary by generated token, evaluating knowledge-intensive question answering and generation.

title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: The Transformer uses attention to process sequences without recurrent or convolutional layers in its proposed architecture. Its encoder-decoder design supports machine translation while enabling more parallel computation during training. The paper evaluates translation quality and also investigates constituency parsing.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: BERT learns contextual text representations by considering information on both sides of a word. Pretrained representations can be adapted to tasks such as question answering and language inference with relatively small task-specific additions. The paper evaluates this transfer across multiple language-understanding benchmarks.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
abstract: Dense Passage Retrieval learns vector representations of questions and passages using two encoders. Retrieval selects passages that are useful for answering a question, providing an alternative to lexical matching such as BM25. The paper evaluates retrieval accuracy and downstream open-domain question answering.

title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
abstract: BART learns to reconstruct text after it has been corrupted. It combines a bidirectional encoder with a left-to-right decoder. The paper compares corruption strategies, including span masking and sentence reordering, and evaluates the pretrained model on text generation and language-understanding tasks.
